slides.texte_overlay:
things you should stop
apologising for

taking up space

stop apologising for sitting down, asking a question or simply being in the room. you belong there just just as much as anyone else in the whole room does.

having needs

stop apologising for needing rest, help or time alone. everyone has needs, and calmly saying yours out loud is a healthy thing, not a selfish or weak one.

not knowing everything

i stopped apologising for what i didn't know and started learning a little every day instead. curiosity feels so much better than constant nervous apologies.
slides.texte_sophia:
not knowing everything

i stopped apologising for what i didn't know. now i take one lesson a day in the Sophia app, a bit of history or science, and every day i know a little more than yesterday.

slides.texte_overlay:
changing your mind

stop apologising for changing your opinion when you learn something new. updating your views isn't weakness, it's proof that you're still learning and growing.

saying no

stop apologising for saying no to things you don't want. a kind no protects your time, and the right people in your life will always understand it and respect it.
